Commentary.Commentary: How will things pan out during the chase? Will West Indies chase this total down easily or will Ireland finish the series with a win? Do join us in a short while to find out.

The target does not look to be a massive one but West Indies did struggle during the chase in the 2nd ODI. They would be eyeing improvement in this area and register a clinical win to complete the clean sweep.

Hayden Walsh is down for an interview with Daren Ganga. Starts by saying it was all about pitching the ball in the right areas. Adds that as the game went on, the ball began to turn more so he tried his variations like the googly. Further says that the ball got a bit older and that is why he got more assistance off the pitch. Ends by saying that they wanted to restrict the Irish to a total of 180 or less but he is confident that his team's batters can knock this target out of the park too.

West Indies were really good with the ball throughout the innings. Oshane Thomas removed the openers early while Roston Chase and Hayden Walsh tightened the screws with their spin bowling. Walsh eventually finished with a 4-fer and stifled Ireland in the middle overs. Romario Shepherd and Alzarri Joseph too were excellent in their spells. Thomas removed the last man to finish with a 3-wicket haul.

A brilliant bowling performance from West Indies means Ireland can only manage a total of 203 runs. Their batting never got going as they kept losing wickets at regular intervals or rather, kept throwing their wickets away. Apart from Andy Balbirnie, the skipper, none of the Irish batters could contribute much with the bat. McCollum, O'Brien and Tucker, were able to get starts but failed to make it count. A 25-run knock off 22 balls from McBrine in the final overs helped them get over the 200-run mark.

Keemo Paul, the substitute, runs across from long off and manages to take the catch. This is a good catch as the long on fielder was also coming across but Paul is conscious of it and makes no mistake. IRELAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 203.

UPDATE - 1010 local (1410 GMT) - As we all hoped, the rain has stopped and the groundsmen are removing the covers now. Seems like both the umpires are doing the inspection right now. Resumption should not be too far away. We will keep you all updated.

We are all set to begin. Paul Stirling and James McCollum make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players follow them out to the field. Romario Shepherd will begin the proceedings.

Pitch report - Daren Ganga says that the last West Indies played here, there were a lot of runs and centuries. Chris Gayle, Jos Buttler scored tons. Darren Sammy says that this pitch is favorable for batters and the bowlers will need to bowl yorkers in the death.

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish skipper, says that they would have bowled first. Adds that it is a good wicket. Boyd Rankin misses out and Craig Young comes in and Gareth Delany makes way for James McCollum.

Kieron Pollard, the West Indian skipper, says that there will be something for the bowlers and wants to give them a chance to test the conditions. Adds that they have made 3 changes. Sunil Ambris comes in for Shimron Hetmyer. Oshane Thomas comes in for Sheldon Cottrell and Roston Chase comes in for Khary Pierre.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, James McCollum (In for Gareth Delany), Andy Balbirnie (C), William Porterfield, Kevin O'Brien, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Simi Singh, Mark Adair, Andy McBrine, Barry McCarthy, Craig Young (In for Boyd Rankin).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Shai Hope (WK), Evin Lewis, Brandon King, Sunil Ambris (In for Shimron Hetmyer), Nicholas Pooran, Romario Shepherd, Kieron Pollard (C), Roston Chase (In for Khary Pierre), Hayden Walsh, Alzarri Joseph, Oshane Thomas (In for Sheldon Cottrell).
Toss - West Indies have won the toss and they choose to bowl first.

A warm welcome to the final ODI between West Indies and Ireland in Grenada. The hosts won a close encounter the last time around, winning by 1 wicket.  That too with the help of some great batting by the lower order. They would now hope that the top order comes good and put in a dominating performance. On the other hand, Ireland improved their performance in the second match taking the match to the very end. Their batting though has been a cause of concern. Andy Balbirnie would want one big innings from one of their batsmen which has not yet happened in this series. There was some overnight rain. Good news is that there is no rain as of now and the match should start on time. Will Ireland end the ODI series on a high or will the hosts complete a whitewash? Stay tuned for the toss and the teams.
